options.description: Execute a command in the new worktree after creation. Arguments after --exec are the command and are passed through, including options. Put the worktree name and other options before --exec

options.name: copy-file
options.description: Extra gitignore pattern of files to copy from the current checkout. Can be used multiple times. Only gitignored matches are copied

options.description: Branch or commit to create the new worktree from (defaults to HEAD)

examples.description: Create a new worktree with an auto-generated name
Create a new worktree named 'feature-auth'
Create a worktree and run npm install
Create a worktree and copy environment files
Create a worktree from main branch
Create a worktree from remote branch

notes: If name is omitted, a random human-readable name is generated automatically
The worktree name will be used as the branch name
Gitignored files matching .worktreeinclude at the checkout root are copied into the new worktree
.worktreeinclude and --copy-file use gitignore syntax. A file is copied only when it matches and is gitignored, so tracked files are never duplicated
Files that already exist in the new worktree are left unchanged
Symlinks are skipped and are not followed. A .worktreeinclude symlink is not read
.ptm.toml is read from the source checkout, the checkout where the command runs. [hooks] post-create commands run in the new worktree, in order, and stop at the first failure
--exec receives PTM=1, PTM_NAME (the worktree name), and PTM_PATH (the absolute worktree path). Post-create hooks also receive PTM_ROOT_PATH (the source checkout path)

notes: By default, deletion will fail if the worktree has uncommitted changes
You can pass multiple worktree names to delete them at once

notes: The command is executed with the worktree directory as the working directory
All arguments after the worktree name are passed to the command, including options. A -- before the command is accepted but not required
The exit code of the executed command is preserved
The command receives PTM=1, PTM_NAME (the worktree name), and PTM_PATH (the absolute worktree path)

preferences.name: preferences

examples.description: Store a custom worktrees directory (relative to the Git repository root) for all commands
Store a separator for flattening worktree directory names while keeping branch names unchanged
Keep branches by default when deleting worktrees with ptm delete
Disable automatic project discovery through ghq

notes: Subcommands:
get <key>    Show a preference value
set <key>    Set a preference value
remove <key> Remove a preference value
Preferences are stored in $XDG_CONFIG_HOME/ptm/config.toml (default ~/.config/ptm/config.toml).
The file and directory are created on the first set. Comments and formatting are preserved.
Supported keys:
worktrees-directory - path relative to the Git repo root for storing worktrees (defaults to .git/phantom/worktrees)
directory-name-separator - replaces '/' in worktree directory names only (defaults to / for nested directories)
keep-branch - keeps the branch when deleting a worktree (defaults to false)
ghq-discovery - discovers ghq-managed repositories as projects (defaults to true)

preferences get.name: preferences get

examples.description: Show the preferred worktrees directory (relative to repo root)
Show the preferred worktree directory name separator
Show whether delete keeps branches by default
Show whether ghq project discovery is enabled

notes: Supported keys: worktrees-directory, directory-name-separator, keep-branch, ghq-discovery

preferences set.name: preferences set

examples.description: Store worktrees in ../phantom-worktrees relative to the Git repository root
Flatten worktree directory names such as feature/test to feature-test
Keep branches when deleting worktrees by default
Disable automatic project discovery through ghq

notes: Supported keys: worktrees-directory, directory-name-separator, keep-branch, ghq-discovery
For worktrees-directory, provide a path relative to the Git repository root; defaults to .git/phantom/worktrees when unset
For directory-name-separator, '/' keeps nested directories; any other string replaces '/' only in the directory path
For keep-branch, use true to preserve branches on delete or false to keep the default branch deletion behavior
For ghq-discovery, use false to list only projects registered directly with Phantom
keep-branch and ghq-discovery are stored as TOML booleans. The other keys are strings.

Restore the default behavior of deleting branches with worktrees
Restore the default behavior of discovering ghq projects

notes: Supported keys: worktrees-directory, directory-name-separator, keep-branch, ghq-discovery

project remove.name: project remove
project remove.description: Remove a Git project from Phantom's registry
notes: The project can be specified by id, name, or root path.
If a name matches multiple projects, use an id or path instead.
This command never deletes the Git repository or its worktrees.
A repository discovered through ghq remains visible after its registry record is removed.
